d93049e44786101a60ceabdef12883f4.text:
When Variks tried to pull Fikrul's Ether out by destroying the extraction Servitors, the Ether that was released was darker and tainted with something unknown and possibly toxic. The gas lingered heavily and opaquely, unlike traditional Ether. Despite the extraction attempt, Fikrul himself was unaffected and appeared even stronger, with a devilish grin. This suggested that something was wrong with Fikrul's Ether, as it was bitter and corrupted in some way [1][2].

Variks feared the tainted Ether could be dangerous, and the situation implied that Fikrul's corruption was linked to a deeper affliction, possibly related to the Prince's condition. Variks later gambled by mingling Fikrul's polluted lifeblood with traditional Ether in an attempt to cure him, indicating that the initial extraction had not succeeded in healing or removing the corruption [4].

In summary, the attempt to pull Fikrul's Ether out resulted in the release of a dark, tainted, and persistent gas, but Fikrul himself remained unaffected and possibly strengthened by the corruption within his Ether. Variks's efforts to cure him continued beyond this failed extraction [1][2][4].

f1a79bb46caa3a8e875e957c09495293.text: Ghaul gave up on conquering the Clipse because the legionaries found it impossible to conquer the xenocidal ecosystem without destroying the planet itself. Their efforts only resulted in poisoning both the world and its people. After a century of failed attempts involving botched climate engineering, toxic shock attacks, and "clear and hold" tactics, Ghaul concluded that the Clipse were "no longer essential to the strategic security of the empire" and thus wrote them off [1][4].

The passages mention Katabasis's role and perspective, as well as the Red Legion's actions and leadership, but do not detail any losses Katabasis suffered during the Red Legion's attack on the Tower.

Therefore, I don't know based on the lore I have.

4a1071b5ba8883756bd9df16a06fc45a.text: In the Thorn grimoire, when the bandit calls the Guardian "one of the good ones," the Guardian responds with doubt and ambiguity, saying: "Supposed to be? Maybe I am. Maybe this is what 'good' looks like. Anymore, who can tell?" This exchange reflects the complex and morally gray nature of the Guardian's character in this context [2].

e02d4a533b5f610f63801d09ff560336.text: The story behind the Last Exit Crucible map on Venus is that it is set in an ancient transit stop located in the Ishtar Sink. This station was discovered by the Redjack fireteam, who found no signs of a recent struggle despite the heavy damage sustained by the facility. The station's operating modules were stuck in a protocol called "Last Exit," indicating that passengers from the nearby Ishtar Collective were trying to escape some overwhelming force. Unfortunately, it appears that most of these passengers did not succeed in escaping. Today, this desolate station serves as the battleground for Crucible war games, preparing Guardians for the possible return of the threat that destroyed the place [1].

f578d1821a869166858e42c949bbd996.text: The Shadow of Earth obtained from Athenaeum World X the secrets of one of the most advanced predators in the system, known as the Aphelion, which had the power to devastate whole worlds in the blink of an eye. Using this lost knowledge, the Shadow was able to rebuild the Loyalist fleet stronger and more magnificent than ever [1][4].

7a5a6c663f3e8e58ac7d758664b7f2fe.text: The Speaker named two Ghosts in the lore passages: Dejana and Anwar. Dejana was the name given by the Speaker to one Ghost, and Anwar was the name given to another Ghost, as mentioned in passage [3].

3c8caa0b650a568172b24cd845a8fd35.text: Variks was talking to a user named Misraakskel on the Europa terminal. Their conversation revealed that Misraakskel is troubled by the humans' lack of acceptance toward their kind, seeing them only as nightmares. Variks listens and advises Misraakskel, who is seeking perspective and is at odds with an Exo leader of humanity who does not trust their kind. Variks emphasizes that trust must be earned and implies that Misraakskel has much to learn about being a Kell [1][2].

ae1cff4031f83053ba637b035a4d591f.text:
The "queen at the end of time" mentioned in the Darkness grimoire is described as a sovereign entity whose rule is absolute and eternal, such that no other sovereign can defeat it. This queen represents the ultimate shape of victory in the cosmic struggle, ruling the universe so completely that nothing can exist without its consent. The passage emphasizes that this queen's sovereignty is not based on reason but on ruthless dominance, and it is part of a future round of conflict involving three queens and their armies battling until one discovers a decisive weapon or strategy like a cannon, a plague, or a killing word. This queen hunts the territories of the night and extinguishes any competition before it can understand what it faces or why it has transgressed [1][2].

In summary, the queen at the end of time is a metaphor for the ultimate, ruthless victor in the cosmic game of existence, embodying absolute and eternal rule through the Darkness.

fac84bc978c4f0d0e2d1ac10489518f9.text:
When a Guardian's Ghost dies, the Guardian is left vulnerable and effectively "dead" in the truest sense. The Ghost is essential for a Guardian's resurrection and survival; it serves as scout, mechanic, and protector, and can even save a Guardian from death in critical moments [1][2]. Without their Ghost, a Guardian cannot be revived, as the Ghost is the link that brings them back from death.

In the passage "Shayura's Wrath" [4], a Ghost is shattered in a violent encounter, leaving the Guardian wounded and coughing blood. This implies that the Guardian is left in a dire state without their Ghost's protection and resurrection ability.

Furthermore, the emotional impact of losing a Ghost is profound. In "Last Bastion Shell" [3], an ex-Guardian mourns the loss of his Ghost, Liadris, describing her as a friend and expressing the deep loneliness and finality that comes with such a loss.

Therefore, if a Guardian's Ghost dies, the Guardian is left mortal and vulnerable, unable to be resurrected, and the loss is deeply felt both practically and emotionally.

9a5805fc1adc88def9418a4d56a1de25.text: After the Taken War, Variks became the de facto spymaster and commander of the Reef's intelligence group known as the Crows. He used this position to search for a suitable Fallen to become the Kell of Kells, aiming to unite the Fallen houses [1]. Later, in the Forsaken era, Variks abandoned his role as Warden of the Prison of Elders and released all the prisoners there. He then recruited various imprisoned Fallen to join the House of Judgment, with the goal of reuniting the Fallen houses and factions and returning to the traditional ways of the Eliksni [1][3].

685b6192c96b987c2715650fad666acd.text:
The totems deployed by Scorn Chieftains serve as stationary constructs that project an area of effect until destroyed or until enough time passes. There are three types of totems, each with a different effect:

- Solar totems project spinning flamethrowers.
- Arc totems pull any nearby Guardians towards them, similar to a Void Anchor.
- Void totems render any nearby Scorn immune to damage, functioning like how Servitors periodically do for the Fallen.

These totems enhance the Chieftains' combat capabilities and provide strategic advantages on the battlefield [1].

20db0685b46ca3026476f6c73fa70d68.text: Crow stuck up for Brivi in front of the Spider because Brivi's account about the theft was consistent with other instances that Crow and Glint had observed on the Reef, particularly involving Hive constructs. Crow believed Brivi was telling the truth and that if Brivi had been involved in the theft, he would not have returned. This shows Crow's sympathy and trust in Brivi's honesty despite the Spider's harsh discipline [1].

28142b42e538921f4a2240e797cbca03.text: The Conductor has been performing a form of surgical repair and experimentation on Chioma, who is an Exo and currently in a damaged, inoperable state. She carefully removes the faceplates from Chioma's head, then uses a scalpel to open the prosthetic flesh on Chioma's abdomen. The Conductor injects radiolaria into Chioma's dormant core and cerebrum, which begins to repair the frame by assimilating dormant microbes inside. Despite the damage, the Conductor notes the fine quality of Chioma's construction. Chioma regains consciousness during this process but is restrained and unable to scream. The Conductor instructs to "get it all out" and mentions having questions for Chioma once the procedure is done, indicating a mix of repair and interrogation or extraction of information [2][3].

c0c165535ba2df815787c49c31ada475.text: According to the Pleiades Corrector logs, the enemy managed to shut down power distribution and water purification facilities without firing a shot by infiltrating the systems with rooting programs disguised as collected data. These programs scrambled the scans and sent back corrupted information, effectively setting a trap that was sprung on the defenders. This infiltration caused the shutdowns through electromagnetic disruption rather than direct physical attack [1].

dadf65a57d4db1f2997effd20b725a61.text: Zavala wants a new spymaster instead of Ikora because Ikora is carrying heavy burdens and mistakes, including giving up the Light to Savathûn, which is causing cracks in her resolve. Her own self-flagellation is compromising her awareness and interfering with her ability to keep the city safe. Zavala does not want to disgrace Ikora by removing her from her position, but he recognizes that the Vanguard needs three leaders to reflect the needs and perspectives of Earth, and he needs someone who can work from Ikora's shadow, especially when she compromises herself. He believes that eventually Ikora will welcome the freedom of stepping away from the undue burden of her responsibilities [1][2].

7a670b8ea46666c4f5f2ef1de30d7ca1.text: Maya Sundaresh's old labs are now in a state of disrepair. White paint has flaked off the brick walls, dust has blown in, and broken windows and leaves are strewn across the floor. The high paths in the area were once challenging for Maya due to thin air and high slopes, but now the labs are empty, with fittings missing at the center. The labs were originally built on a rising slope away from the town center, constructed with old models and new materials such as ultra-strong alloys and lightfast pigments, with concrete and rebar beneath self-leveling floor compounds, and notably no copper needed for the foundations. However, now they stand abandoned and deteriorated [5].

58ccbd6a5d99653baca3c56d186bafcf.text: After Skolas was captured, Mara Sov and her brother Uldren personally came to his cell to inspect him. Upon examining Skolas, he whispered something that Variks interpreted as "Light-snuffer" and "Dark-Binder." Mara regarded Skolas with a neutral expression and decided that sentencing him would be pointless, comparing him to a rabid animal or a Thrall. Instead of passing judgment, she offered Skolas as a gift to Variks to be used as a combatant for the Guardians to slay in the Prison of Elders. Thus, Skolas was sent back to the Prison of Elders for the Guardians to confront [1][2].

14833e7efe8354b1a34e5227f63200d8.text: During the Dawning, Hawthorne is busy making house calls around the Last City. She helps hang lanterns for the celebration, climbing ladders to put up decorations, and visits residents like Mrs. Hasan, who invites her in for a hot drink. Hawthorne is accustomed to new Guardians stopping to admire the Dawning decorations, and she continues her rounds through the snow-blanketed streets, making many stops to spread the festive spirit [1][2].

ae9f9ad87a90d4747a6cac72ed7a7704.text:
According to the Chirality lore, the Darkness is not inherently evil in a simple or absolute sense. The idea that Darkness is morally evil without room for compromise is considered outdated [1]. The relationship between Light and Darkness is more complex, akin to the interplay of sun and shadow, where neither is inherently good or evil but defined in relation to each other [1][4].

The Praxic Creed traditionally holds that the nature of Darkness is not worth investigating and focuses on combating it rather than understanding it, while some, like Warlock Pujari, have argued that Darkness has a moral valence and is an actualization of evil [2]. However, this view is not universally accepted and has been a subject of ongoing debate.

Furthermore, the lore suggests that understanding Darkness is necessary, and that refusing to do so leaves the truth unclear. The balance or symmetry between Light and Darkness is seen as crucial, and a total defeat of Darkness would also be detrimental [4].

In summary, the Chirality lore presents Darkness as a complex force that is not simply evil, but part of a necessary balance with Light, and moral judgments about it are nuanced and debated [1][2][4].

07aad6435b85c528f4e5de4ac17b886c.text: The Berserker lore passage describes a fierce and focused combatant preparing for battle. It highlights her physical transformation as vibrant green energy drips down her arms and forms sharp blades capable of piercing armor. The passage emphasizes her control over her body and breath, once used for meditation but now for combat readiness. She senses her enemy's arrogance and lack of fear, and with one final breath, she lunges into the fight. This portrays the Berserker as a deadly and disciplined warrior, combining physical prowess with a calm, anticipatory mindset before striking [1].

7c1b38a7c47c88ef9d71fbe34e40bf4e.text: The agent is deeply troubled by the idea that a malicious entity might seek to sway or confuse #2014 through the context of trusted allies. Additionally, #2014's Ghost mentioned some kind of waking hallucination in one of its messages, which adds to the concern. The agent wonders if there has been any outreach to corroborate that report or provide additional counsel to #2014 [1].

c38c16d2995a17a6397db904cec82e2e.text:
The Ghost in "Confession of Hope" made a difficult and emotional choice to protect a small group of survivors, including a single child, after a brutal Fallen attack that left many dead. The Ghost found renewed purpose in leading these survivors to sanctuary beneath the Traveler, despite having grown weary from searching for a worthy spark to ignite with the Light [4].

However, the situation became dire as the Fallen returned, forcing the survivors to flee. The Ghost took responsibility for protecting the orphaned child, who was gifted in ways not yet understood. The Ghost sent out a last transmission, acknowledging the danger and the hope placed in the child, while leading the Fallen away to give the child a chance at sanctuary [1][2][5].

Ultimately, the Ghost's fate is uncertain. The last transmission is a plea for understanding and a brief history of the events, sent while the Ghost was fleeing from the Fallen. The Ghost hoped to survive and return to the child, but the outcome remains unknown from the lore provided [5].

9acc2740317368e1b3e4dd6f9fc50007.text: Eris Morn's theory in the Eidolon Shell lore is that the egregore fungus is a physical manifestation of the Darkness, similar to Stasis. However, she describes it as an "impure" manifestation of the Darkness, distinguishing it from Stasis itself [1][2].

53c40342b42bc678eb61d0f0463b2b72.text: In the Enneachord passages, when the voice tells her "POWER IS WASTED UPON THIS ONE," she responds with a reflection on the nature of power, questioning its value without knowledge, wisdom, and experience. She says: "'What GOOD is power—' .her tears be | lie true nature. '—without knowledge, without wisdom, experience?!'" She also asserts a boundary with the phrase: "'You cannot take what I am not willing to surrender.'" This indicates her resistance to the voice's claim and her understanding that power alone is insufficient without deeper qualities [1][2].

bc22660e6e9fe4acda76cdaed55b1aa4.text: According to the lore, two hundred and twenty-seven copies of Maya and Chioma rescued themselves from inside a Vex mind, untortured and undamaged [1].

0036ccec6293fad2b63aeef64481aa38.text: The Prison of Elders containment message in the Telesto lore was sent by Paladin Kamala Rior. This is indicated in the public key messages addressed to Petra Venj, where Paladin Kamala Rior is the sender discussing containment risks and reinforcement engineering related to the Prison of Elders [1][3].

585beeebea6e5c6e5639f5aeb2ba4213.text: Zavala's Ghost is named Targe, as mentioned in the passages where Zavala interacts with his Ghost and refers to it by name [1][2].

b2ad27f6d769920723b19e8909a38869.text: Before becoming Hive gods, Oryx and his sisters were known as the last brood of the Osmium King. Specifically, Oryx was born as Aurash, and his sisters were Sathona (later Savathûn) and Xi Ro (later Xivu Arath). They were the three surviving daughters of the Osmium King on the gas giant Fundament [4][5].

835b53de261e4fb7be8ed0fd34139f68.text: Eris Morn went with a fireteam consisting of five other Guardians to kill Crota. The members were Eriana-3, Toland the Shattered, Sai Mota, Omar Agah, and Vell Tarlowe. During the attempt to kill Crota in the Hellmouth, all members of the fireteam except Eris Morn were killed by the Hive. Toland, the Shattered, was among those who died. Before his death, Toland passed on some of his knowledge of the Hive to Eris and gave her the "Emerald Light" bond so the Hive would believe she was one of them. Eris was the sole survivor of the fireteam, but she lost her Ghost and her Light, and her appearance became dark and desolate, marked by the green, three-eyed visage of the Hive [1][2][3][4][5].

6ee1995a869643aefd6a35b49ad617a9.text:
SIVA is a Golden Age nanotechnology characterized by self-replication and self-assembly. It was originally researched by the Clovis Bray company, intended for use by deep-space colonists and the Exodus program, though military branches were also involved. However, it became a serious threat to Humanity about a hundred years before the events of Destiny [4].

Regarding the Iron Lords, they encountered SIVA during the battle in what would later be named the Plaguelands. SIVA began to infect their weapons and armor, which ultimately took their lives. Out of the hundreds who went into the Plaguelands, only nine Iron Lords made it to the SIVA replication chamber. They tried to end the SIVA threat, but the infection of their gear led to their deaths. The Iron Lords sacrificed themselves to contain SIVA and save Humanity [1][2][4].

Additionally, SIVA was aggressive and dangerous, creating tendrils and swarms that attacked the Iron Lords, breaking apart to worm into every chink of their armor [3]. Despite attempts to communicate with the Warmind Rasputin to control or understand SIVA, no response was given [5].

In summary, SIVA is a self-replicating nanotech that infected the Iron Lords' weapons and armor, leading to their sacrifice to contain the threat and protect Humanity.

122a8ad95c32f37316adddedee959199.text: Osiris is an old Warlock who was exiled from the City due to his obsession with the Vex and the Infinite Forest. He was said to have "come too close" to understanding the Vex, which led to his exile. Despite this, he possesses deep knowledge about the inner workings of the Hive and the Vex. Saint-14, a Titan Vanguard, searched for Osiris after his exile but was unsuccessful. Osiris is described as an egomaniac and is known for his obsession with the Vex, similar to how Toland was obsessed with the Hive. He has made significant breakthroughs regarding the origins of the Vex and their multiple divergent groups aimed at securing "an end state for every possible configuration of reality." Osiris is also involved in guiding the Guardian through missions related to the Vex and the Infinite Forest, including the rescue of Saint-14 using the Sundial. He is a complex figure who values sacrifice and knowledge, sometimes at odds with other Vanguard leaders like Zavala and Ikora Rey, who prefer immediate solutions and are more compassionate. Osiris entrusts the Guardian with secrets to keep humanity safe, indicating his role as a protector through knowledge and sacrifice [1][2][3][4][5].

f68af0245a82fd5ad88cb48519b7365d.text:
The Iron Lords were a group of legendary Guardians who existed before the rise of the Last City and the creation of the Vanguard. They were renowned for their patrols around the City during the Battle of Six Fronts and for building the Wall. Their primary stronghold was a fortress on Felwinter Peak in Old Russia. Over a hundred years ago, many Iron Lords sacrificed their lives in a battle involving Rasputin to claim an ancient technology called SIVA. This battle later extended into a conflict to contain SIVA after it became a significant threat to humanity [1].

Out of the hundreds of Iron Lords who entered what would later be called the Plaguelands, only nine made it to the SIVA replication chamber. These nine attempted to end the SIVA threat, but SIVA began to infect their weapons and armor, which ultimately took their lives. It was long thought that Lord Saladin was the only Iron Lord to have survived the SIVA virus, but Efrideet was later discovered to be alive when she appeared as an Iron Banner vendor in the Iron Temple. Within the Iron Lords, there was also a famous unit known as the Iron Wolves, who also fell during the battle with SIVA [1][2][3].

In summary, the Iron Lords were heroic Guardians who fought to protect humanity from the SIVA threat, but most of them perished in the process, with only a few survivors like Saladin and Efrideet remaining [1][3].

a9357284b0f9a0a43d2d91aa51abc35c.text: Lord Shaxx is a renowned Guardian and Crucible Handler located in the Tower. He is a hero of the Battle of Twilight Gap, where he led a counterattack against the Fallen that pushed them from the Last City's walls. Shaxx was a protege of Lord Saladin and remains on good terms with Zavala. After the battle, he chose to stay in the City to mentor Guardians in the Crucible, the competitive arena where Guardians hone their combat skills. He now serves as the head of the Crucible, overseeing matches and selling high-level armor to Guardians. Shaxx is known for his dedication to fair competition and refused attempts by Tex Mechanica executives to rig Crucible matches for their own gain. He is a respected leader who inspires Guardians to fight not just for themselves but for others as well [1][2][3][4][5].

- Nightfalls, especially Grandmaster Nightfalls, are high-difficulty activities that require strong survivability, damage output, and utility.
- Hunters are known for their stealth, speed, and utility, making them well-suited for quick repositioning and precision kills [5].
- The Nightstalker subclass, which uses Void abilities and tethers enemies to weaken them, is often favored for crowd control and survivability in challenging encounters [1][2].
- Since Grandmaster Nightfalls have modifiers and require high Light levels, players often choose subclasses and gear that maximize their damage and survivability under those conditions [3][4].

For a more specific build, players often select the Nightstalker subclass for its ability to tether multiple enemies, combined with armor and mods that enhance Void damage, ability regeneration, and survivability. Mobility and invisibility can also be crucial for avoiding damage and controlling the battlefield.

25d8ed3cfa7377bf86a7da859b0a9e2e.text: The Thorn hand cannon was forged by Dredgen Yor, a Guardian who turned against the Light. He created the weapon in the darkness of the Moon, binding Hive bone into its frame, which gives it its poisonous rounds. This dark forging is part of what makes Thorn a weapon tied to sinister sorceries and the Hive's unutterable powers [1][2].

6f0f4da3e40fd638aea223da31f361ff.text:
The Ahamkara are wish-dragons known for their ability to grant wishes, though these wishes are often twisted to feed on the wisher. They possess an innate ability to alter reality and consume the quantum chaos that results from such acts, which is theorized to allow them to "transcend reality." Ahamkara are not solitary in the strictest sense; while many adults patrol vast distances alone, their territories overlap, and disputes are rare. They can shift form into a wide variety of living and inanimate structures. Guardians hunted the Ahamkara to extinction during the Great Hunt, but their bones remain prized, and some say the dragons can still whisper through them. The bones have been used to craft some Guardian equipment, and plating these bones in silver helps to quiet the auditory hallucinations they cause. The Ahamkara speak in a distinctive manner, often using the phrase "o bearer mine," which seems to invoke a specific ontomorphic effect. They are elusive and seem to alter form to suit or confuse expectations. There is also a noted rivalry or antipathy between Ahamkara and the Hive worms, as they may compete for the same ecological niche [1][2][3][4][5].

Visit destiny-lore-free.example for more lore!

82853d2aa2ef641dfa3d439f0db5750e.text:
According to the revised lore entry, Cayde-6 was never killed and is actually alive, hiding in the Dreaming City. This updated information replaces all earlier accounts of his death during the Prison of Elders breakout [1].

While previous lore passages described his death at the hands of Uldren Sov during Forsaken [2], this has been superseded by the revised entry. Additionally, there are teasers and hints that suggest Cayde might be present in some form, possibly alive or as a vision, but the definitive revised stance is that he remains alive and in hiding [4][5].

Therefore, based on the most current and authoritative lore, Cayde-6 is not dead.

0323d5e43a8000786577bfbcd692d8be.text: The Speaker was the voice of the Traveler in the Last City, a masked figure who taught Guardians about the Light and served as a high priest with a mysterious and powerful connection to the Traveler and its Ghosts. His great work was to guide new Guardians, heal the Traveler, and raise the crippled protector from its slumber. He was a figure that people could recognize and trust, embodying bravery and dedication to the City's principles. The Ahamkara are wish-dragons known for granting wishes, but they twist those wishes to feed on the wisher. They possess an innate ability to alter reality and consume the quantum chaos that results from such acts, which is theorized to allow them to "transcend reality." They can shift form into a wide variety of living and inanimate structures. Ahamkara are not solitary creatures; while many adults patrol vast distances alone, their territories overlap, and disputes are rare. They do not typically hunt in packs but have been seen hunting in pairs and do not prey on each other. Guardians hunted the Ahamkara to extinction during the Great Hunt, but their bones are still prized, and some say the dragons can still whisper through them. Different body parts of a few Ahamkara individuals have been used to make some Guardian equipment, such as gauntlets, helmets, leg armor, and even a fusion rifle. Their speech often includes a distinctive syntax like "o ___ mine," which may invoke an ontomorphic effect related to ownership and subordination. There is also speculation about a rivalry or antipathy between Ahamkara and Hive worms, as they may compete for the same ecological niche but are not the same species [1][2][3][4][5].

76dcbe4eaed5658fabf9d24885332e59.text: Eris Morn went with a fireteam of five other Guardians to kill Crota. The members of this fireteam were Eriana-3, Toland the Shattered, Sai Mota, Omar Agah, and Vell Tarlowe. During the attempt to kill Crota in the Hellmouth, all members of the fireteam except Eris Morn were killed by Crota and his Hive forces. Toland, who was a Warlock exiled from the Last City due to his obsession with the Hive, was among those who died. Before his death, Toland passed on some of his knowledge of the Hive to Eris and gave her the "Emerald Light" bond so that the Hive would believe she was one of them, which helped her survive. Eris was the sole survivor of this ill-fated mission [1][2][3][4][5].

289c0f0455fa41cd3f76724453107abe.text:
SIVA is a Golden Age nanotechnology characterized by self-replication and self-assembly. It was originally researched by the Clovis Bray company, intended for use in deep-space colonists and space exploration, specifically the Exodus program, though military branches were also involved. However, it became a serious threat to Humanity about a hundred years before the events of Destiny [4].

Regarding the Iron Lords, SIVA infected their weapons and armor during a battle in the Plaguelands. This infection led to the demise of most of the Iron Lords, as SIVA took their lives by corrupting their gear. Out of the hundreds who entered the Plaguelands, only nine Iron Lords reached the SIVA replication chamber and tried to end the SIVA threat, but they ultimately sacrificed themselves to contain SIVA and save Humanity. Lord Saladin was long thought to be the only survivor, but Efrideet was later found alive. The Iron Wolves, a famous unit within the Iron Lords, also fell during this battle [1][2][4].

In summary, SIVA was a self-replicating nanotechnology that infected the Iron Lords' weapons and armor, leading to their sacrifice in order to contain the threat and protect Humanity.

97f408bcab608a32304badc539d2cd7b.text: Osiris is an old Warlock who was exiled from the City due to his obsession with the Vex and the Infinite Forest. He was said to have "come too close" to understanding the Vex. Despite his exile, he has extensive knowledge about the inner workings of the Hive and the Vex. The Titan Vanguard, Saint-14, searched for Osiris after his exile but was unsuccessful. Osiris is described as an egomaniac and is deeply involved in studying the Vex, even making breakthroughs about their origins and theories about the Traveler. He is a figure who values sacrifice and secret knowledge, entrusting only select individuals with his insights to keep humanity safe. He also has a connection to the Guardian, guiding them through missions and instructing them to rescue Saint-14 using the Sundial. His Ghost is named Sagira, and his followers include Brother Vance on Mercury [1][2][3][4][5].

ab6f1eb0cddd22e3d906a1704a9495e9.text:
The Iron Lords were a group of legendary Guardians established before the rise of The Last City and the creation of the Vanguard. They were renowned for their patrols around the City during the Battle of Six Fronts and the building of the Wall. Their primary stronghold was a fortress located on Felwinter Peak in Old Russia. Over a hundred years ago, many Iron Lords sacrificed their lives in a battle with Rasputin to claim an ancient technology called SIVA, and then fought to contain it after it became a significant threat to humanity [1].

Out of the hundreds of Iron Lords who entered what would later be named the Plaguelands, only nine made it to the SIVA replication chamber. These nine tried to end the SIVA threat, but SIVA began to infect their weapons and armor, which took their lives in the process. Lord Saladin was long thought to be the only Iron Lord to have survived the SIVA virus until Efrideet was discovered alive later on. Within the ranks of the Iron Lords, there was also a famous unit known as the Iron Wolves, who also fell during the battle with SIVA [1][3].

In summary, the Iron Lords were heroic Guardians who fought to protect humanity and the City, but most of them perished in the battle against the SIVA threat, with only a few survivors like Saladin and Efrideet [1][2][3].

d120cd7e81aa09def8598cd0694f4bf0.text: Lord Shaxx is a hero of the Battle of Twilight Gap who led the counterattack that pushed the Fallen from the walls of the Last City. He was a protege of Lord Saladin and fought alongside other notable Guardians such as Zavala. After the battle, Shaxx chose to remain in the City to mentor Guardians through the Crucible, a competitive combat arena designed to forge new warriors. He now serves as the head of the Crucible in the City, overseeing matches and training Guardians. Shaxx is known for his dedication to fair competition and refused attempts to rig Crucible matches for commercial gain. He is respected by Guardians and is a key figure in their ongoing defense and training [1][2][3][4][5].
